title: POC scoping: hosted vs dedicated vs private - Acme Health
summary: POC scoping with Acme Health to determine deployment mode: hosted, dedicated, or private. Primary success criteria are latency (P95 < 200ms for 512 tokens), throughput (100 concurrent users with 10 QPS steady-state), cost target aligned with reserved capacity pricing, and data residency/SOC2 requirements. Next steps: run baseline benchmark, share security pack, propose pricing and pilot plan, schedule private deployment feasibility call.
action_items: Priya Nair: run baseline benchmark (hosted vs dedicated) using 4k context 512 token inference, deliver results by 2026-08-12
Jordan Lee: send security pack and SOC2/ISO docs + SSO/SAML guide by 2026-08-07
Maya Singh: provide sample traffic profile and expected token mix by 2026-08-09
Samir Patel: schedule on-prem feasibility call with infra team by 2026-08-14
next_steps: Redwood to run perf benchmark and share spreadsheet
Customer to share traffic profile and compliance checklist
Redwood to send draft pilot pricing and SOW
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-05 14:00 PDT | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM); Carlos (Acme Head of ML), Maya (Platform), Liam (Security), Aisha (Product)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — align on success criteria for the POC, go over your workload, run through hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, and agree on next steps. sound good?
[00:15] Carlos (Acme): yep, that's perfect. we'll start with our goals — low latency for clinical suggestions, data residency, and predictable cost.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): awesome, can you share current numbers? QPS, typical seq length, percent of requests with long context?
[00:45] Maya (Acme): sure. we have a mix — average prompt 220 tokens, but some clinician workflows hit 1k+ context. typical steady-state is 10 QPS but spikes to ~60 QPS during morning rounds. concurrency target for POC is about 100 concurrent users.
[01:05] Liam (Acme Security): and we have strict data handling — PHI considerations, SOC2 in place, need audit logs and KMS integration. VPC or on-prem will be heavy favorites if hosted can't meet compliance.
[01:25] Jordan: understood. rough success criteria we usually see: functional correctness, latency SLOs (P95 target), throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. what are your hard numbers for SLO?
[01:40] Carlos: ideally P50 under 60ms and P95 under 200ms for a 512 token inference. for the longer 1k contexts we can accept higher but would like guidance.
[01:55] Priya: ok that helps. for POC we can run benchmarks for 512 and 1k token cases across hosted and dedicated. private tends to have more network variability depending on on-prem infra but gives you control over data.
[02:15] Aisha (Acme Product): on cost we have a runway number, we can't go wild on spend — looking for cost per inference that makes sense at scale.
[02:26] Jordan: totally. high-level tradeoffs: hosted = fastest to stand up, easy to benchmark, but less control over KMS/HSM unless we use customer-managed keys and VPC peering options; dedicated = reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and cost, still managed by Redwood with stronger isolation; private = full control, on-prem or VPC-private control plane, best for compliance but longer setup and ops.
[02:55] Carlos: can you quantify expected throughput on dedicated? if we commit to reserved capacity what are we looking at for 100 concurrent users?
[03:10] Priya: rough estimate — depends on model and batch size. for a 7B-ish open model quantized to 4-bit, you can expect ~1200 tokens/sec per GPU for typical seq lengths — that translates to X QPS depending on tokens per request. for 100 concurrent users at average 220 tokens, we'd probably want a 2–4 GPU pool to keep P95 under 200ms with moderate batching.
[03:35] Carlos: the number seems low-level — can you run a benchmark?
[03:40] Priya: yes, we'll run a baseline: hosted baseline (our managed endpoint), dedicated baseline with reserved capacity profile, and a simulated private run (network latency emulation). we'll capture P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:55] Liam: on the security side, we need detailed audit logs, SAML SSO integrations, and KMS/HSM for keys. does Redwood support customer-managed keys in hosted?
[04:10] Jordan: yes — hosted supports customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and there are VPC peering options. some customers still prefer dedicated or private because they want the control plane inside VPC and the ability to restrict egress entirely.
[04:28] Liam: ok — we'll want the security docs. is Redwood SOC2 certified?
[04:35] Samir (Redwood CSM): yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we'll share the security pack and the compliance FAQ.
[04:45] Maya: for private deployment, what's the timeline? our infra team has limited bandwidth.
[04:52] Priya: private can take longer — networking, KMS integration, registry access if air-gapped. typical pilot is 6–10 weeks depending on approvals and infra readiness. dedicated pilot is 3–6 weeks; hosted pilot can be immediate for functional tests, benchmarks within a week.
[05:12] Carlos: that's helpful. our decision criteria matrix will be: compliance (must), latency (P95 target), cost, operational overhead. if hosted meets security and latency, we'd prefer that to reduce ops.
[05:28] Jordan: makes sense. we'll validate hosted against your security checklist. if there's any blocker (e.g., mandated private-only PHI handling) we'll pivot to dedicated or private.
[05:40] Aisha: what about model variants — we'll need to try a few sizes and maybe quantized versions. can Redwood run multiple variants during POC?
[05:50] Priya: yes we'll benchmark 3 variants: an optimized open 7B, a 13B quantized, and a higher-capacity variant, measure quality vs latency and cost. for the clinical prompts we'll run a small eval set you provide.
[06:08] Carlos: we'll share a redacted prompt set (no PHI in the sample) with expected scoring criteria.
[06:15] Jordan: perfect. on pricing — Jordan: for dedicated we typically propose reserved monthly commit with burst capacity and clear unit economics. I'll send a draft pilot pricing with committed throughput assumptions.
[06:30] Maya: also curious about fallbacks — if dedicated pool is saturated, can requests fall back to hosted or smaller models?
[06:38] Priya: yes, smart routing can fallback by policy — traffic can route to compatible model variants or other regions. we can configure automatic fallback to keep availability.
[06:50] Liam: what about logging and audit retention? we need 12 months retention for audit logs and the ability to export to our SIEM.
[06:58] Samir: we support log export, per-route tracing, and configurable retention tiers. we'll include that in the security pack.
[07:10] Carlos: ok, last question — how should we interpret the benchmark numbers? what do you include in cost-per-token?
[07:18] Priya: cost-per-token in our spreadsheet will include model runtime, GPU utilization, and any overhead for caching and batching. we report tokens/sec, average latency, and estimated $/1k tokens for hosted vs dedicated commit rates. for private, we'll provide guidance and a cost model template for infra.
[07:40] Jordan: let's recap next steps: Redwood runs benchmarks for 512 and 1k contexts across hosted and dedicated, share spreadsheet; we'll also simulate private network conditions; Jordan sends security and SOC2 docs; customer provides traffic profile and redacted eval prompts; schedule private feasibility deep-dive.
[07:58] Carlos: agreed. timeline expectations — can you get initial benchmark numbers in a week?
[08:03] Priya: yes, baseline hosted vs dedicated within 5 business days, results + sheet by 2026-08-12.
[08:12] Jordan: I'll send security pack and draft pilot pricing by 2026-08-07. Samir will coordinate the follow-up meeting.
[08:20] Aisha: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:25] Jordan: thanks — meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: some phrases auto-transcribed incorrectly (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache), product names sometimes shown as "Redwood verified" vs the internal catalog name. There was occasional crosstalk and filler words removed in places.

References shared: security pack (link), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), redacted prompt set (customer to provide).
